question: Which of the following alterations in amino acid metabolism is caused by a deficit of vitamin B12 ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "impaired conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA" -> "accumulation of methylmalonic acid" -> "methylmalonic acidemia" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "disruption in amino acid metabolism" -> "possible accumulation of metabolites" -> "unclear if related to other options" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "inhibition of methylation reactions" -> "increased levels of methylmalonic acid" -> "methylmalonic acidemia" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "altered metabolism of certain amino acids" -> "methylmalonic acid accumulation" -> "methylmalonic acidemia" -> 85%
analysis: Vitamin B12 is essential for the conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA. A deficiency in vitamin B12 leads to the accumulation of methylmalonic acid, resulting in methylmalonic acidemia. The other options are related to different metabolic disorders not directly linked to vitamin B12 deficiency.
